title: Anorectal manometry
what: A thin soft tube, called a catheter, is put into your back passage. It measures how the muscles of your rectum and anus work.
why: For constipation, leaking stool, before some operations, and after childbirth if you have these problems.
duration: usually 30 to 45 minutes; results are given right away or in a few days
tell_doctor: If you had surgery on the rectum
If you have a painful fissure or hemorrhoids

prepare.title: Cleansing
prepare.text: Often a small enema is done 1 to 2 hours before the test. The clinic will give you instructions.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no special diet is needed. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: You are sometimes asked to skip laxatives and some other medicines. Do not stop anything on your own. Ask your doctor.

steps: You lie on your left side with your knees to your chest
The doctor puts a thin catheter with gel into your back passage
You are asked to relax, squeeze your muscles, and push
Sometimes a small balloon is inflated in the bowel, and you are asked what you feel
feel: You may feel an urge to go to the toilet
It can feel awkward. That is normal. The doctor does this every day
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
Results are explained right away or in a few days
red_flags: Bleeding from the back passage that does not stop
Severe belly pain or a temperature above 38°C (100.4°F)

faq.a: Usually not. The catheter is thin. It is more unpleasant than painful.
It shows the doctor whether your muscles work properly when you go to the toilet.

reminders.text: Anorectal manometry tomorrow. Check whether you need an enema before the test, and when.
